# <span id="aanchor120"></span> About Meters

A meter is a physical device used in the field to measure the flow of gas and liquid products. Each meter type has unique identifiers and characteristics. FLOWCAL supports several meter types, including cone, Coriolis, orifice, positive displacement, turbine, and ultrasonic.

#### Meter Types

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Cone">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Cone Meter</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Cone">

Cone meters use a conical position inside of the pipe to cause a pressure drop. The amount of the pressure drop is used to calculate the amount of mass and volume being moved.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 219;height: 85;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Coriolis">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Coriolis Flow Meter</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Coriolis">

Coriolis flow meters use vibrating tubes to calculate the mass and density of the product passing through it.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 193;height: 73;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Line Pack">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Line Pack</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Line Pack">

Line pack meters are used to monitor pipeline inventory. Line pack meter periodics reflect pipeline inventory at a particular time period. The meter rollup process calculates changes in pipeline inventory from one period to the next.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 172;height: 170;" />

See: [Line Pack Meters](Line%20Pack%20Meters.md)

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Orifice">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Orifice</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Orifice">

Orifice meters use a plate in a pipe to cause a pressure drop. The amount of the pressure drop is then used to calculate the amount of mass and volume being moved.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 136;height: 135;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Positive Displacement">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Positive Displacement</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Positive Displacement">

Positive displacement meters are a type of rotary meter. The container is filled with fluid and rotates from supply side to distribution side. Each rotation creates a pulse which correlates to a fixed amount of volume.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 143;height: 126;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Turbine">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Turbine</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Turbine">

Turbine meters have a fan blade in the pipe that rotates as product passes through it. Each rotation results in a pulse. These pulses are used to calculate the amount of volume passing through the pipe.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 178;height: 96;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Ultrasonic">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Ultrasonic</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Ultrasonic">

Ultrasonic meters use ultrasonic transmitters and receivers to calculate the velocity of the liquid passing through. This is used to calculate the volume.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 191;height: 97;" />

</div>
